chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hammad ibn Bashir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The fulfilment [of the transaction] does not occur until the scale inclines [tilts in favour of the buyer].

key_terms.الْمِيزَانُ: The scale or balance used for weighing

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for the scale to 'incline' in a trade transaction according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi is often interpreted not merely as a commercial recommendation but as a spiritual principle of generosity (ihsan), where the seller intentionally tilts the scale to give the buyer a slight excess. This 'inclination' symbolizes the perfection of the transaction, ensuring that the buyer feels fully satisfied and that the seller's intent is pure, reflecting the broader Islamic ethic of going beyond strict justice. It highlights the transition from mere legal compliance (adl) to moral excellence (ihsan) in daily interactions.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bakeyr, from Hammad Bin Basheer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The fulfilment does not occur unless the ‘scale’ inclines (tilts in favour of the buyer)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Hammad ibn Bashir who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Proper weighing is only when a balance tilts to one side.”’
